title: Lecture 6: Cell division
summary: The four phases of mitosis in order, with the midterm hint that anaphase is where sister chromatids are pulled apart.

sections.title: Prophase
bullets: The nuclear envelope breaks down; the spindle forms from the centrosomes.

sections.title: Metaphase
bullets: Chromosomes line up along the middle: the metaphase plate.

sections.title: Anaphase (on the midterm)
bullets: Sister chromatids are pulled apart to opposite poles.

sections.title: Telophase
bullets: Prophase in reverse: nuclear envelopes re-form around each set of chromosomes.

examFlags.text: This one will be on the midterm, by the way: anaphase is where the sister chromatids get pulled apart.
examFlags.why: The lecturer said it will be on the midterm.

items.prompt: Your lecturer said this will be on the midterm: what happens in anaphase?
items.answer: The sister chromatids are pulled apart to opposite poles.

items.prompt: Where does the spindle form from?

items.answer: The line along the middle of the cell where the chromosomes line up in metaphase.
